reason: The cold preparation enclosure seems like the natural place to prepare a clear view while keeping the core frozen. It is also the only offered action.
expectation: I expect the core to be placed or prepared in the cold enclosure, though I don't know exactly how it will be exposed.

effect: The flat optical face provides a clear view while leaving the speck untouched, so the next task is to illuminate and examine it.
reaction: The closed cover and untouched speck make the preparation feel careful and satisfying.
reason: The field lamp seems useful for illuminating the prepared face, and it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the lamp to light the band for closer inspection, though I don't know whether that will resolve the speck by itself.

effect: Backlighting reveals a folded outline and projections deep inside the band, but a closer view is still needed.
reaction: The outline makes me curious about what the speck is.
reason: The cold microscope is the only offered combination and seems suited to resolving the speck while keeping the core frozen.
expectation: I expect a magnified view of the folded speck, though I don't know how much detail it will reveal.

effect: The microscope confirms a whole articulated body in the ice and shows why preserving the frozen core mattered: its posture and surroundings remain visible.
reaction: The confirmation is striking, especially alongside the damaged first specimen.

mostWorthwhile.text: Examining the core under the cold microscope was most worthwhile: it revealed the whole body and made the value of preserving its context clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the lamp was the least engaging action because it was the only available combination, though the backlit outline built curiosity.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the folded speck resolved into a whole, long-dead body, with its limbs and position preserved in the ice.

arbitrary.text: None felt arbitrary; each action had a clear purpose in preparing, illuminating, or examining the core. The choices were all forced, though.

continue.text: Yes. I would choose to continue because I want to learn how Earth responds to the discovery and what further study reveals.
